The following data come from an experiment investigating the crispiness of cookies. The researchers studied the effects of temperature, studied at two levels (325°F and 350°F), and the amount of flour, studied at three levels (2 cups, 2.25 cups, and 2.5 cups).

The response variable of interest was cookie crispiness, measured as the amount of force (in Newtons) required to break the cookie in half. Three cookies were baked separately for each treatment combination.

The crispiness measurements for each cookie are shown below.

| Temperature | 2 cups     | 2.25 cups  | 2.5 cups   |
| ----------- | ---------- | ---------- | ---------- |
| 325°F       | 78, 74, 75 | 85, 86, 86 | 72, 75, 73 |
| 350°F       | 79, 82, 82 | 89, 87, 86 | 71, 70, 68 |

## a. Identify the structure of the experiment

:::

![](../_images/4.1-cookie-blueprint.png)
:::

**Treatment structure**

:::{.version-instructions .version-student}
  + Name of the treatment structure: ________________________
  + Factors + Levels: ________________________
  + t = ______
  
:::

:::{.version-instructions}
\vspace{0.15in}
:::

:::{.version-solution}
    + Name of the treatment structure: 2 x 3 full factorial
    + Factors + Levels: Temperature (325$^{\circ}$ F and 350$^{\circ}$ F), Flour (2, 2.25, and 2.5 cups)
    + t = 6
:::


**Experimental structure**

:::{.version-instructions .version-student}
+ Randomization method: ______
+ Experimental unit (e.u.): ________________________
  + r = ______
+ Measurement unit (m.u.): ________________________
  + N = ______

:::

:::{.version-instructions}
\vspace{0.15in}
:::


:::{.version-solution}
    + Randomization method: CRD
    + Experimental unit (e.u.): one cookie
      + r = 3
    + Measurement unit (m.u.): one cookie
      + N = n = 18
:::

## b. Set up notation for treatment means

Let $y_{ijk}$ represent the observed crispiness for the $k^{th}$ cookie baked at the $i^{th}$ temperature with the $j^{th}$ amount of flour.

:::{.version-instructions .version-student}
For i = _____________, j = _________________, and k = ________________
:::

:::{.version-instructions}
\vspace{0.15in}
:::

:::{.version-solution}
For i = 1,2, j = 1,2,3 , and k = 1,2,3

:::

## c. Compute treatment-combination means

Compute the mean crispiness for each treatment combination and record your values below.

:::{.version-instructions .version-student}

| Temperature | 2 cups     | 2.25 cups  | 2.5 cups   |
| ----------- | ---------- | ---------- | ---------- |
| 325°F       |            |            |            |
| 350°F       |            |            |            |
:::

:::{.version-instructions}
\newpage

:::


::: {.cell version='solution'}

```{.r .cell-code}
ybar11. <- mean(c(78, 74, 75))
ybar12. <- mean(c(85, 86, 86))
ybar13. <- mean(c(72, 75, 73))
ybar21. <- mean(c(79, 82, 82))
ybar22. <- mean(c(89, 87, 86))
ybar23. <- mean(c(71, 70, 68))
```
:::


:::{.version-solution}
| Temperature | 2 cups     | 2.25 cups  | 2.5 cups   |
| ----------- | ---------- | ---------- | ---------- |
| 325°F       | 75.67|85.67 | 73.33|
| 350°F       | 81| 87.33| 69.67 |
:::




## d. Simple effects of temperature (holding flour constant)

For each flour level $j$, compute the simple effect of temperature, i.e. our **estimate** for:

$$\mu_{1j}-\mu_{2j}$$

:::{.version-instructions .version-student}
+ $j=1$: _____________________________
+ $j=2$: _____________________________
+ $j=3$: _____________________________
:::

:::{.version-solution}
+ $j=1$: -5.33
+ $j=2$: -1.67
+ $j=3$: 3.67

:::

Interpret the estimated simple effect for $j = 1$ in context of the cookies.

:::{.version-instructions}
\vspace{0.8in}
:::

:::{.version-solution}
At 2 cups of flour, we estimate that cookies baked at 350 are on average 5.3 newtons of force crispier than cookies baked at 325.
:::

## e. Main effect of temperature

Compute the main effect of temperature (i.e. our estimate for $\mu_{1\cdot}-\mu_{2\cdot}$). 

_________ - ________ =

:::{.version-instructions}
\vspace{0.15in}
:::

:::{.version-solution}
$\bar y_{1\cdot\cdot} - \bar y_{2\cdot\cdot}$ = 78.22 - 79.33 = -1.11
:::



Interpret this estimated contrast value in context.

:::{.version-instructions}
\vspace{0.8in}
:::

:::{.version-solution}
We estimate that cookies baked at 350 are on average 1.11 newtons of force crispier than cookies baked at 325.
:::

## f. Main effect of flour amount

Compute *two* main effects contrasts comparing flour levels. Clearly show notation ($\mu_{ij}$).

:::{.version-instructions}
\vspace{0.8in}

\newpage
:::

:::{.version-solution}

There are three possible main effects of flour amount (you could flip the order of subtraction):

  - $\mu_{\cdot1} - \mu_{\cdot2}$
  - $\mu_{\cdot1} - \mu_{\cdot3}$
  - $\mu_{\cdot2} - \mu_{\cdot3}$
  

::: {.cell}

:::

  
  
  
1. For the contrast  $C = \mu_{\cdot1} - \mu_{\cdot2}$:

$\hat C = \bar y_{\cdot1\cdot} - \bar y_{\cdot2\cdot} =$ 78.33 - 86.5 = -8.17 

2.  For the contrast  $C = \mu_{\cdot1} - \mu_{\cdot3}$:

$\hat C = \bar y_{\cdot1\cdot} - \bar y_{\cdot3\cdot} =$ 78.33 - 71.5 =6.83 

3.  For the contrast  $C = \mu_{\cdot2} - \mu_{\cdot3}$:

$\hat C = \bar y_{\cdot2\cdot} - \bar y_{\cdot3\cdot} =$ 86.5 - 71.5= 15 

:::


## g. Interaction: difference of differences

+ By hand (or using excalidraw.com), draw an interaction plot of the treatment means.

:::{.version-instructions}
\vspace{2in}
:::

:::{.version-solution}
![](../_images/4.1-cookie-interaction.png)
:::

+ Visually, does there appear to be evidence of interaction? Explain briefly.

:::{.version-instructions}
\vspace{0.8in}
:::

:::{.version-solution}
There does not appear to be too strong of an interaction effect (we will test!). The trends in crispiness seem to be similar (produces crispier cookies than 325) with the slight exception of 2.5 c. of flour. Additionally, 2.25 c. flour produces crispier cookies than 2 c or 2.5 c.
:::

+ Compute the interaction contrast comparing flour levels 2 cups and 2.5 cups. Clearly show notation ($\mu_{ij}$).

:::{.version-instructions}
\vspace{0.8in}
:::

:::{.version-solution}
$$
\begin{align*}
  C &= (\mu_{11} - \mu_{21}) - (\mu_{12} - \mu_{22}) \\
    &= 1 \mu_{11} + -1 \mu_{12} + 0 \mu_{13} + -1 \mu_{21} + 1 \mu_{22} + 0 \mu_{23}
\end{align*}
$$

$\hat{C} = (\bar y_{11\cdot} - y_{21\cdot}) - (\bar y_{13\cdot} - y_{23\cdot})$ = -9

:::

+ Interpret this value in context. What question is this contrast answering?

:::{.version-instructions}
\vspace{0.8in}
:::

:::{.version-solution}
We estimate that the average change in crispiness due to temp (325 vs 350) at 2c. of flour is 9 newtons less than the average change in crispiness due to temp at 2.5c. 
:::
